svg.text: Tamagi 1.0 — What Changed & How Updates Work
Visual guide to systemd-boot + composefs, /var/home preservation, native Chromium, and transactional updates
CLEAN INSTALL REQUIRED (ISOS BEFORE 2026-11-23)
Why must older machines reinstall from the new ISO?
• Tamagi switched from GRUB + /boot ext4 (ostree) to systemd-boot + composefs.
• bootc cannot convert existing GRUB disks to systemd-boot in place during normal updates.
• Older installations still boot and get updates, but miss tamagi harden strict,
tamagi update changes, and the Secure Boot kernel guard.
→ Installed from the 2026-11-23 ISO or newer? NO reinstall needed:
just run tamagi update as usual.
Your personal files can be preserved!
Inspired by openSUSE Aeon, the new installer detects your
existing /var/home or /home automatically:
✓ Legacy Tamagi layout (ostree + /boot + LUKS2)
✓ Btrfs subvolumes (home / @home) or dedicated /home partition
✓ Reattaches Snapper snapshots and keeps UID/GID & SELinux
Tip: always keep an external backup before repartitioning.
1. WHAT CHANGED IN ARCHITECTURE
Boot, Hybrid ISO & Reliable USB Media
• dracut-initqueue hang fixed: ISO built with
xorriso -partition_offset 16
giving partition 1 a valid ISO9660 label.
• Lean live initramfs: trimmed heavy host-only modules, added
explicit USB drivers + rd.luks=0 rd.lvm=0 rd.md=0 on media.
• Verified USB writer: live/write-usb.sh wipes old metadata,
uses Direct I/O (oflag=direct) and verifies bit-by-bit off cache.
• English boot & Secure Boot: English GRUB/Plymouth defaults;
MOK key universalblue.der + diagnostics GRUB boot entry.
sudo bash live/write-usb.sh /dev/sdX --yes
Aeon-Style /var/home Preservation
• Read-only probe: the installer scans disks safely for
home, @home, legacy ostree homes, or dedicated /home partitions.
• LUKS2 compatible: prompts for your passphrase to unlock
encrypted volumes without formatting and re-seals TPM 2.0.
• /efi + /boot merge: merges legacy ext4 /boot into the ESP
for systemd-boot and migrates via Btrfs reflink with zero copy cost.
• 1st-boot reconnect: preserves existing UID/GID, SELinux labels,
and reattaches your .snapshots subtree to Snapper.
tamagi-detect-home · firstboot --no-create-home
Btrfs + Snapper Armored Against Collapse
• Strict separation: bootc owns the OS (/); Snapper manages
ONLY /var/home/<user>. Root Snapper configs are blocked.
• Isolated subvolumes: var-containers, var-flatpak, var-cache,
and var-log stay mounted separately so root never bloats.
• Games & Flatpaks excluded: .local/share/Steam, flatpak,
lutris, containers, and VMs become excluded subvolumes.
• Auto space pruning: clears old snapshots and orphan objects
(composefs-gc) before staging updates when free space < 15 GiB.
tamagi doctor · home-snapshots prune 15
Transactional Updates + Native Chromium
• Race-free lock (flock): if the 6h timer is staging an update,
running tamagi update waits cleanly without lock collisions.
• transactional-update features: check, drop, rollback, history,
--reboot, --soft-reboot, pre/post hooks, and async layer rebuilds.
• Checkpoint sync: creates pre-update home snapshot so
tamagi rewind aligns OS, apps, and files on every upgrade.
• Pre-installed Chromium + WebApps: ships native chromium +
chromedriver, Google Account OAuth2 sign-in & ChromeOS PWAs.
tamagi update [--reboot|--soft-reboot] · drop · history
2. CLEAN INSTALL WALKTHROUGH (PRESERVING HOME)
Backup & Flash ISO
List your Flatpaks and back up
important files externally:
flatpak list --app --columns=app
Write the new ISO to USB:
sudo bash live/write-usb.sh /dev/sdX --yes
UEFI Boot & MOK
Boot from the USB drive in UEFI.
First boot with Secure Boot enabled,
inside blue MokManager screen:
Enroll key → universalblue.der
MOK Password: universalblue
Preserve /var/home
When picking your target disk, the
installer detects your old install
(asks passphrase if LUKS2).
Pick "Keep files (/var/home)"
to replace only OS & bootloader
while keeping your personal data.
1st Login & Health
Enter the same username as before
to reconnect your home folder
and Snapper snapshot history.
Then verify system health:
tamagi doctor && tamagi snap
3. DAILY UPDATE WORKFLOW
Atomic Update Lifecycle (Without Breaking the OS)
Automatic every 6 h (skips battery/metered links) or on-demand via tamagi update.
1. Pre-flight & Home Checkpoint
An flock lock prevents timer races; prunes old snapshots &
composefs-gc (< 15 GiB), then takes a pre-update snapshot.
2. Signed Download & Secure Boot Guard
Verifies cosign signature, checks quarantine, and stages quietly.
Aborts automatically if Secure Boot is on without enrolled MOK.
3. Side-by-Side Staging + Apps & Boxes
New image is staged (running OS untouched); Flatpaks, boxes, and
AI agents update. Preview diffs with tamagi update changes.
4. Atomic Boot Switch (or Soft-Reboot)
On reboot (or via --reboot / --soft-reboot), the new version
activates; the previous OS remains selectable in systemd-boot.
5. Post-Boot Self-Healing & Async Layer Rebuild
If core checks fail: 1st strike disables layers and retries;
2nd strike runs bootc rollback + quarantine. When healthy,
tamagi-layer-rebuild.service updates sysexts in idle.
Day-to-Day Commands (tamagi update & rewind)
Everything you need to check, inspect, stage, switch, or undo an update.

g.text: Update OS image, layers, Flatpaks, boxes, and AI
Check registry for a new image without downloading
Show package & kernel diff + local AI summary
Timers, booted & staged digests, and free space
Update everything and reboot if a new OS is staged
Fast userspace switch (full reboot if kernel changed)
Discard a staged OS update before rebooting
Queue the previous OS deployment for next boot
Inspect update, drop, rollback & quarantine log
Prune unused images, composefs-gc & old snapshots
